'''Sergiu Klainerman''' (born May 13, 1950) is a [[mathematician]] known for his contributions to the study of [[hyperbolic differential equation]]s and [[general relativity]]. He is currently the [[Eugene Higgins]] Professor of Mathematics at [[Princeton University]], where he has been teaching since 1987.

==Biography==
He was born in 1950 in [[Bucharest]], [[Romania]], into a [[Jews|Jewish]] family. After attending the [[Tudor Vianu National College of Computer Science|Petru Groza High School]],<ref name="Ziare">{{cite news|url=https://ziare.com/international/stiri-internationale/sergiu-klainerman-nu-este-suficient-sa-aparam-libertatea-de-exprimare-si-neutralitatea-o-strategie-de-aparare-a-culturii-occidentale-e-necesara-1629593|title=Sergiu Klainerman: Nu este suficient să apărăm libertatea de exprimare și neutralitatea. O strategie de apărăre a culturii occidentale e necesară|lang=ro|publisher=Ziare.com|date=September 7, 2020|access-date=August 16, 2024}}</ref> he studied mathematics at the [[University of Bucharest]] from 1969 to 1974. For graduate studies he went to [[New York University]], obtaining his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1978.<ref name="vita">{{cite web| url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/~seri/homepage/SergiuCV.pdf|title=Sergiu Klainerman's Curriculum Vitae}}</ref> His thesis, written under the direction of [[Fritz John]] and [[Louis Nirenberg]], was titled ''Global Existence for Nonlinear Wave Equations''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=18856}}</ref> From 1978 to 1980 Klainerman was a [[Miller Research Fellows|Miller Research Fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], while from 1980 to 1987 he was a faculty member at New York University's [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], rising in rank to Professor in 1986.<ref name="vita" />

Klainerman is a member of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] (elected 2005),<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200507/people.pdf National Academy of Sciences elections], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 52 (2005), no. 7, p. 764</ref> a foreign member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] (elected 2002)<ref>[http://www.academie-sciences.fr/membres/K/Klainerman_Sergiu.htm Sergiu Klainerman bio page] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091129083838/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/membres/K/Klainerman_Sergiu.htm |date=2009-11-29 }}, [[French Academy of Sciences]]. Accessed January 13, 2010.</ref> and a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (elected 1996).<ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/199607/people.pdf American Academy Elections.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303225244/http://www.ams.org/notices/199607/people.pdf |date=2016-03-03 }} [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 43 (1996), no. 7, p. 781</ref> In 2003, he was awarded the [[National Order of Merit (Romania)|Romanian Order of Merit]], Commander rank.<ref>{{citation| url=https://legislatie.just.ro/Public/DetaliiDocument/44401| title=Decret nr. 370 din 11 iunie 2003| language=ro|work=[[Monitorul Oficial]]| issue=420|date=June 16, 2003|access-date=May 28, 2025}}</ref> He was elected to the 2018 class of [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2018 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2017-11-03}}</ref>

He was named a [[MacArthur Fellow]] in 1991<ref>[http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.1142705/k.28E8/Fellows_List__July_1991.htm MacArthur Fellows, July 1991] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929090935/http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.1142705/k.28E8/Fellows_List__July_1991.htm |date=2007-09-29 }}, [[MacArthur Foundation]]. Accessed January 13, 2010.</ref> and [[Guggenheim Fellow]] in 1997.<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=k&page=10 Fellows list], {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110603234941/http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=k&page=10 |date=2011-06-03 }} [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|Guggenheim Foundation]]. Accessed January 13, 2010.</ref>
Klainerman was awarded the [[Bôcher Memorial Prize]] by the American Mathematical Society in 1999  "for his contributions to nonlinear hyperbolic equations".<ref name="bocher"/> He is currently a co-Editor-in-Chief of [[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]].<ref>[https://www.ihes.fr/jsp/site/Portal.jsp?page_id=29 Editorial Board], [[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]]. Accessed January 13, 2010</ref>

==Major publications==
*{{Cite journal|last=Klainerman|first=Sergiu|year=1980|title=Global existence for nonlinear wave equations|journal=[[Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics]]|volume=33|issue=1|pages=43–101|doi=10.1002/cpa.3160330104|mr=0544044}}
*{{Cite journal|last1=Klainerman|first1=Sergiu|last2=Majda|first2=Andrew|author2-link=Andrew Majda|year=1981|title=Singular limits of quasilinear hyperbolic systems with large parameters and the incompressible limit of compressible fluids|journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics|volume=34|issue=4|pages=481–524|doi=10.1002/cpa.3160340405|bibcode=1981CPAM...34..481K|mr=0615627}}
* Klainerman, Sergiu; Majda, Andrew. ''Compressible and incompressible fluids.'' Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35 (1982), no. 5, 629–651. 
* Klainerman, Sergiu. ''Global existence of small amplitude solutions to nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations in four space-time dimensions.'' Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985), no. 5, 631–641.
* Klainerman, Sergiu. ''Uniform decay estimates and the Lorentz invariance of the classical wave equation.'' Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985), no. 3, 321–332.
* Klainerman, S. ''The null condition and global existence to nonlinear wave equations.'' Nonlinear systems of partial differential equations in applied mathematics, Part 1 (Santa Fe, N.M., 1984), 293–326, Lectures in Appl. Math., 23, Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI, 1986.
* Klainerman, S.; Machedon, M. ''Space-time estimates for null forms and the local existence theorem.'' Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 46 (1993), no. 9, 1221–1268.
* Klainerman, S.; Machedon, M. ''Smoothing estimates for null forms and applications.'' A celebration of John F. Nash, Jr., [[Duke Mathematical Journal]] 81 (1995), no. 1, 99–133 (1996).
* Klainerman, Sergiu; Sideris, Thomas C. ''On almost global existence for nonrelativistic wave equations in 3D.'' Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 49 (1996), no. 3, 307–321.

==Books==
* [[Demetrios Christodoulou|Christodoulou, Demetrios]]; Klainerman, Sergiu. ''The global nonlinear stability of the Minkowski space.'' Princeton Mathematical Series, 41. [[Princeton University Press]], Princeton, NJ, 1993. x+514 pp. {{ISBN|0-691-08777-6}}
* Klainerman, Sergiu; Nicolò, Francesco. ''The evolution problem in general relativity.'' Progress in Mathematical Physics, 25. Birkhäuser Boston, Inc., Boston, MA, 2003. xiv+385 pp. {{ISBN|0-8176-4254-4}}
